title: guv-calcs v0.9.0: An open-source Python library for modeling germicidal UV in indoor environments
description:
guv-calcs is an open-source Python scientific computing library for physically based modeling of germicidal ultraviolet (GUV) light in indoor environments, with a focus on far-UVC (200–235 nm) applications. The library provides core numerical tools for representing lamps, spatial geometry, calculation planes and volumes, and exposure metrics such as irradiance, fluence rate, and cumulative dose.

The package implements vectorized radiative transfer calculations using measured photometric data (IES/ULD files), supports flexible three-dimensional room geometries, and is designed for integration with higher-level tools such as visualization dashboards, airflow models, and risk frameworks for airborne pathogen control. The codebase emphasizes reproducibility, transparency, and modularity so that researchers, engineers, and manufacturers can inspect, extend, and validate the underlying calculations.

guv-calcs forms the computational backbone of the broader Illuminate ecosystem, but is usable as a standalone library for custom analyses, batch simulations, and method development. The project aims to improve rigor and accessibility in far-UVC modeling by providing a free, auditable, and community-maintained alternative to proprietary software.

v0.9.0 Release Notes

Added

  • Fixture.mount_face (HousingFace: top/bottom/front/back/left/right, default top: the face against the wall or ceiling; the beam points away from it), Fixture.roll (0/90/180/270) and Fixture.emitter_offset (x, y, z from the mounting point, in housing axes, any sign; None = emitter on the front face): the housing box is described in its own frame and can sit anywhere relative to the emitter; Lamp(mount_face=, housing_roll=, emitter_offset=), Lamp.update_fixture(**changes), Fixture.aim_bounds()/aim_corners()/aim_to_housing_extents()

Changed

  • The housing box always contains the luminous opening (LM-63 width x length x height around the photometric center), and a lamp's default housing is the full luminous opening including its height; by default a 3D opening sits flush with the housing's front face, so its photometric center is half the opening's height inside. Fixture.aim_bounds/aim_corners take `luminous=(length, width, height)`; LampGeometry.aim_bounds() and LampPlacer clearances include the opening
  • Fixture.photometric_depth is derived from emitter_offset: the distance from the front face back to the emitter (still accepted by Fixture(), Lamp() and from_dict, may be negative)
  • LampPlacer.ceiling_offset and wall_clearance use the housing box's real extent around the emitter

Fixed

  • Total power (Lamp.get_total_power, and scaling to a total power) overcounted IES files with unevenly spaced angles, such as upper-room fixtures sampled densely around 90°: a Lumalier 150 file read 4535 mW instead of 273 mW. Requires photompy 0.3.1
